ratings_why.fun: Placement is a real puzzle every turn and the late game pays out big, but the tribe's own stats grow slowly from Tier 3 to Tier 5, so the mid-game climb feels thin.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because its damage is the enemy's own Attack turned on itself, so it gets stronger as the lobby does; no current tribe or typical auto-battler tribe works like that.

verdict_why: Nothing is broken or unreadable; the hot spots (the Lantern wall, Ignis, the Steward) are tuning for the owner, and more passes would only reshuffle cards.

points.text: Permanent stats from Tier 3 to 5 come only from Joan and the Lost readers, so the board can look small against big mid-game boards. One more modest grower for Lantern carriers at Tier 4 would smooth the curve.
Stingy Jack is the engine of the Lamp Row wall. If playtests hit the lock, cap carriers at 2 permanent Lanterns before touching Jack's price, so the 2-gold trade stays.
Old Will with Black-Water Reflection is the climb's best moment: their carry doubles into their other carry. Keep it as the spike; it is what makes the tribe worth reaching Tier 6 for.
Settle with the rules whether Start of Combat Stones change who attacks first; the Stones build's tempo depends on it.
Captain Spunkie's Tier 6 Refreshes fix his dead text well; he is a fine econ piece that mostly gets sold once the capstones arrive.

standouts.why: Old Will turns random friendly fire into chosen friendly fire: the seed's 'decide what the enemy hits' as one rule.
Black-Water Reflection is a clean multiplier that scales with the enemy's own power, the right job for Tier 4.
Hoard Mere Light turns the enemy's drowned stats into yours, so the payoff keeps pace with the lobby's biggest boards.

weakest.why: Fresh-Ink Mapseller is a capped gold trickle with no tie to placement; it does the expected Tier 2 economy job and nothing more.
Gaffer Turncoat is mostly a mirror tech line plus a one-off swap; in most lobbies it's a vanilla Tier 3.
Little Phos is a fine seed, but at three times a fight it tops out early and gets sold by Tier 4.

flags.note: Turnips plus Old Will can put 3 Lanterns on all four front units: 12 misled attacks before the enemy touches you, while it hits itself. Counters are few.
Ignis Fatuus has no cap: with 12+ misleads a fight it gives about 140 stats a turn, top of the Tier 6 range, and golden doubles it.
Brass-Badge Steward reads uncapped Lost, so a full Lantern wall gives +12/+12 or more a turn at Tier 4, about twice the target.
Half the stats of every drowned enemy, against the lobby's biggest boards, can mean very large buried totals late.
